title: Minimax Testing of Positive Probability of Necessity under Monotone Treatment Response
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4; supported composite n^(-1/3) and flat (log n)^(3/4)/sqrt(n) testing results graded incremental below the field floor, salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: The testing headlines themselves are supported: cross-resolution orthogonality leaves coefficients dependent only on coarser signs, and the rough-null comparison controls full fixed-sample mixtures rather than merely matching singleton laws.

The projected score is constrained by the single known-uniform, quarter-Hölder benchmark, incomplete positioning against one-smooth-margin product problems, and constants that make the stated upper guarantees vacuous across extensive finite-sample ranges; the clinical citation supplies motivation rather than demonstrated practical calibration.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: The original honest-interval angle duplicated an active quarter-cone run, so an authorized seeded switch produced composite positive-PN testing under unknown quarter-Holder propensity and unrestricted prognosis. Discovery discharged matching n^(-1/3) composite and (log n)^(3/4)/sqrt(n) simple-flat testing frontiers, but the independent general score 6.3 fell below the field floor 7.4 and capped the result at incremental. No Lean formalization was launched; the sound informal package is retained for lower-tier re-anchoring.
tldr: The whole-composite-null positive-PN testing frontier is proved at \(n^{-1/3}\), with no logarithmic or other slowly varying factor, by the original-record projection upper test and a legal rough-null paired-mixture converse. For every \(n\ge2\), the matched bounds are \(V_n(1024n^{-1/3})\le1/10\) and \(V_n(2^{-24}n^{-1/3})\ge4/5\). The distinct simple-flat-null frontier is \(s_n=(1+\lceil\log_2(n^2)\rceil)^{3/4}/\sqrt n\), which is asymptotically strictly smaller; hence \(P_\star\) is not rate least favorable. Unrestricted prognosis signs at rough no-attribution laws create the additional composite obstruction. These finite testing results provide a benchmark for the causal-attribution question studied by Tian--Wu, rather than a claim about the covariate design of their application.
gap: The closest conditional-independence testing result imposes conditional regularity absent from the maintained prognosis class. Regular PN inference also relies on nuisance-product control. Flat-null calibration alone cannot establish composite-null level.
fill: Close the explicit \(n^{-1/2}\)-to-\(n^{-1/3}\) finite testing bracket using one-sided multiresolution calibration and legal original-record mixture converses, resolve every slowly varying factor, and determine whether the flat comparison law represents composite-null difficulty.
